profile.reading: Per DC BLOX's own site, this Chattanooga, Tennessee facility sits at 807 East 16th Street and currently operates 8,000 square feet of data center space (expandable to 16,000 square feet) plus up to 2,000 square feet of tenant office space, supporting up to 1 MW of critical load today, expandable to 3.5 MW. The facility runs dual 1,600-amp smart-grid utility service, N+N generator backup with 36-hour on-site fuel storage, N+N UPS with dual feeds to all cabinets, N+1 cooling via a 280-ton air-cooled chiller plant and 240-ton high-efficiency dry cooler plant with hot-aisle containment, and is built with a precast concrete shell and reinforced concrete data hall slabs; the operator markets it as a Tier III colocation facility offering 50U lockable cabinets, turn-key and build-to-suit options, and high-density deployments, though no specific third-party certification (such as an Uptime Institute award) is listed on the operator's own page for this facility, unlike DC BLOX's Birmingham and Myrtle Beach sites tracked elsewhere in this registry. DC BLOX operates a network of data centers across the Southeast United States; per the company's own data center map page, it operates 23 facilities totaling 2,780,376 square feet and 470 critical MW company-wide, a company-level aggregate this registry does not apply to this individual facility's own figures above. No year-opened date was located in sourcing reachable this session. No public ownership structure or investor detail specific to DC BLOX was located in sourcing reachable this session. DC BLOX positions itself as a regional Southeast US colocation and network fabric provider rather than a national hyperscale operator, emphasizing secondary and tertiary metro markets like Chattanooga, Birmingham, Huntsville, and Myrtle Beach that larger national operators have historically underserved, a strategy distinct from the dense Northern Virginia or Silicon Valley clustering seen among many other operators tracked in this registry.

Across Tennessee, this site ranks fifth by published capacity among four facilities that disclose power figures, but the state context reflects only 12.13 MW of published capacity across all mapped data centers in Tennessee, making statewide disclosure sparse.

The facility's power capacity is not published. Without a disclosed megawatt figure or square footage broken to this address, no calculation of rack or accelerator density is possible from the operator's own specifications.
